'''Gabriel Oltramare''' (19 July 1816 – 10 April 1906) was a Swiss mathematician, known for his book ''Essai sur le Calcul de Généralisation''.<ref name="Dictionnaire">{{HDS|31994|author=Martin Kurz|date=3 November 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Lovett, E. O.|authorlink=Edgar Odell Lovett|title=Review of ''Calcul de Généralisation'' par G. Oltramare|journal=Bulletin of the New York Mathematical Society|volume=6|date=December 1899|pages=109–113|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1899-00684-0|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Oltramare, G.|title=Calcul de généralisation|year=1899|location=Paris|publisher=A. Hermann|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=hvd.32044091888420;view=1up;seq=11}}</ref>

==Biography==
Oltramare was born in [[Geneva]] on 19 July 1816, the son of cousins Anne Oltramare and Louis-David-Benjamin Oltramare, a [[watchcase]] maker.<ref name=Dictionnaire/> He belonged to a prominent family of Italian [[Protestant]] origin that settled in Geneva in the 16th century.<ref>{{HDS|25546|Oltramare|author=Marie Bron|date=2 December 2010}}</ref> Oltramare studied mathematics and natural sciences in Geneva from 1836 to 1839, then studied higher mathematics at the [[University of Paris Faculty of Humanities|Sorbonne]], graduating with a ''[[Licentiate (degree)#France|licence ès sciences mathématiques]]'' in 1840.<ref name=Dictionnaire/> He was a teacher in [[Aarau]].<ref>{{cite book|editor=Bölling, Reinhard|title=A photo album for Weierstrass|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=1994|page=31|isbn=9783528066024|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sBTHA11BODsC&pg=PA31}}</ref> From 1843 to 1844, Oltramare worked in Egypt as a tutor for [[Isma'il Pasha|Isma'il]], son of [[Ibrahim Pasha of Egypt|Ibrahim Pasha]] of the [[Muhammad Ali dynasty]]. He was ''[[Privatdozent|privat-docent]]'' of mechanics at Geneva's industrial school from 1845 to 1870, as well as professor of mathematics at the [[Collège Calvin|Collège de Genève]] from 1848 to 1850. In 1848, Oltramare was appointed professor ordinarius of higher mathematics at the [[University of Geneva|Academy of Geneva]].<ref name=Dictionnaire/> 

At the beginning of his career he did research on number theory, on which he published several works;<ref name=Dictionnaire/> according to [[Henri Fehr]], the most important of these is the 1855 ''Note sur les relations qui existent entre les formes linéaires et les formes quadratiques des numbers premiers''.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Fehr, Henri|title=Gabriel Oltramare. 1816–1906|journal=Actes de la Société Helvétique des Sciences|volume=89|year=1906|url=https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=sng-005:1906:89::894|format=PDF}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Oltramare, Gabriel|title=Note sur les relations qui existent entre les formes linéaires et les formes quadratiques des numbers premiers|journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik|volume=49|year=1855|pages=151–160|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=hvd.32044102910528;view=1up;seq=169}} [http://eudml.org/doc/183386 European Digital Mathematics Library eudml.org record]</ref> Later in his career Oltramare worked on mathematical analysis. In 1893 he published his treatise ''Essai sur le calcul de généralisation'', with 2nd edition in 1899 and a Russian translation in 1895. He published several articles on astronomy and meteorology in scientific journals. He was one of the founders in 1853 of the ''Institut national genevois'' and presided from 1894 to 1902 over its section of natural sciences. He was a member in 1848 of the ''Conseil administratif de Genève'' and member from 1848 to 1854 of the [[Grand Council of Geneva]], over which he presided several times.<ref name=Dictionnaire/> He was one of the organizers of the first [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], which was held in Geneva in 1897.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Rudio, F.|editor-link=Ferdinand Rudio|title=Verhandlungen des ersten Internationalen Kongresses in Zürich vom 9. bis 11. August 1897|page=6|publisher=BG Teubner|year=1898|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=umn.319510001714689;view=1up;seq=20}}</ref>
